claude.sample_unit: contents and responses (71 website contents, 213 standard and 213 simplified ChatGPT-4 responses)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of standard ChatGPT-4 patient education responses versus websites
links.effect: Standard ChatGPT-4 responses required grade 10 and higher by FKGL (e.g., Healthline-matched 11.26 vs website 8.86), above typical patient reading levels.
links.quote: Standard ChatGPT-4 responses consistently required a reading level of grade 10 and higher according to the FKGL metric across all examined websites.

links.outcome: Readability of responses when prompted for sixth-grade level versus standard prompt
links.effect: Simplified prompt lowered FKGL to about sixth to seventh grade (e.g., 6.64 vs 11.26 standard) with accuracy similar to websites.
links.quote: The simplified ChatGPT-4 responses consistently exhibited a pattern where the required reading comprehension level, as determined by the FKGL metric, corresponded to sixth to seventh grade ( Table 5 ).

links.outcome: Response quality and readability when prompt varied by requested literacy level
links.effect: Adding a sixth-grade request changed reading level substantially; accuracy remained comparable to websites, but comprehensiveness and preference ratings dropped versus standard responses (e.g., preference 3.62 vs 4.59 for Healthline comparison).
links.quote: The simplified ChatGPT-4 responses matched existing websites in terms of personal preference, accuracy, and comprehensiveness.

unlisted_practices: Prompting a general-purpose LLM to generate patient education at a target reading level

links.outcome: Specialist ratings versus existing patient-education websites
links.effect: Standard ChatGPT-4 preference 4.37–4.59 vs websites 2.90–3.45; comprehensiveness 4.40–4.78 vs 2.00–3.13; accuracy similar, all P>0.05.
links.quote: It was found that trained specialists preferred the standard responses provided by ChatGPT-4, and perceived these responses to be more comprehensive while maintaining accuracy compared with contents from the existing websites ( Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Readability of simplified patient education responses
links.effect: Simplified ChatGPT-4 FKGL was 6.08–7.03 across sources versus standard 10.25–11.26 and existing websites 7.05–9.67.
links.quote: The simplified ChatGPT-4 responses consistently exhibited a pattern where the required reading comprehension level, as determined by the FKGL metric, corresponded to sixth to seventh grade ( Table 5 ).

links.outcome: Grade level of patient education materials
links.effect: Simplified responses were targeted to sixth-grade comprehension and had FKGL 6.08–7.03 across source-matched question sets.
links.quote: In contrast, simplified ChatGPT-4 responses were more accessible, suitable for a sixth- to seventh-grade level.

links.outcome: reading level of standard ChatGPT-4 responses
links.effect: Standard ChatGPT-4 responses consistently required a reading level of grade 10 and higher across all examined websites, with Flesch-Kincaid Grade Levels ranging from 10.25 to 11.26.
links.quote: Standard ChatGPT-4 responses consistently required a reading level of grade 10 and higher according to the FKGL metric across all examined websites.

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4 responses for patient education on uveitis and specifically compares standard prompts to prompts with a reading-level constraint (sixth-grade comprehension level) to assess readability, accuracy, and comprehensiveness.
